project: CRYPTO-22 — KeyPackage attestation (ephemeral MLS leaf ↔ DID leaf-binding) — umbrella #2187
description: CRYPTO-22 (#2187) replaces the non-standard MLS leaf==DID conflation with an ephemeral, context-scoped leaf signature_key plus an #active/#agent-signed KeyPackage attestation that binds all four leaf public keys to the member's DID (§9.7.1, §9.5.2; ADR-057 Amendment 2026-08-01). The program lands as slices S1–S7. S1 (the pure 0xFF03 data type + §9.5.1 serialization + §25.23 Vector 37 KAT) and S2 (the pure 13-check verifier core verify_attestation, checks 3–13, deliberately deferring the two resolution-dependent checks 1–2 to the runtime caller — merged as PR #2246) are already on main in crates/scp-mls/src/keypackage_attestation.rs. This PRD file is the CRYPTO-22 program home; it currently authors only S4. NOTE (observation, not authored here): S1–S3 shipped without PRD stories — a program-level provenance gap; those retroactive stories are out of scope for this artifact and are not fabricated here.

gates.name: Verifier resolve + current-key freshness seam (§9.7.1 checks 1–2)

stories.title: Implement the two caller-deferred KeyPackage-attestation verifier checks (§9.7.1 checks 1–2): a pure wasm-safe current-key + freshness seam in scp-mls (Layer A) and an async DidResolver-backed, Add-fail-closed seam in scp-runtime (Layer B)
stories.description: Implement the two verifier checks that the merged S2 pure core (verify_attestation, §9.7.1 checks 3–13) deliberately defers to the runtime caller — §9.7.1 checks 1 (the signing_key_id names the DID's CURRENT #active/#agent verification method; a rotated-away or #retired-* key MUST NOT verify — rotation is revocation, §9.12) and 2 (the DID document used to satisfy check 1 MUST be no older than MAX_ATTESTATION_KEY_RESOLUTION_STALENESS = 300s, §9.18.7 — a bound decoupled from and far tighter than the §9.10.7 privacy-cache TTL of 24h/7d). The merged S2 code documents this exact caller contract on AttestationVerificationContext::resolved_current_vm_pubkey and on verify_attestation's rustdoc ('This is what a later wiring slice (S4/S6/S7) MUST enforce before calling'). Build the seam in two layers, per the SCP wasm-safe / async split (ADR-057). LAYER A (pure, wasm-safe, in the existing crates/scp-mls/src/keypackage_attestation.rs module): a deterministic side-effect-free function that, given the attestation, an ALREADY-RESOLVED scp_did::DidDocument, that document's resolution timestamp (resolved_at, Unix seconds), and now (Unix seconds), plus the remaining leaf/credential ground-truth fields — first enforces check 2 (reject with a typed staleness error when now.saturating_sub(resolved_at) > MAX_ATTESTATION_KEY_RESOLUTION_STALENESS), then enforces check 1 (extract the current verification-method public key named by the credential's signing_key_id from the resolved document via the existing ScpCredential::resolve_signing_key path — reject when that VM is absent/#retired-* in the current document), then constructs the AttestationVerificationContext with resolved_current_vm_pubkey set to that extracted current key and delegates UNCHANGED to verify_attestation for checks 3–13 (so a rotated-away key surfaces as the existing check-3 SignatureInvalid). Layer A does NO I/O, NO DID resolution, and NO clock read — resolved_at and now are caller-supplied, keeping it wasm-safe and reusable by the browser client. LAYER B (async, in scp-runtime): a function that resolves the signer's DID via the canonical scp_identity::resolver::DidResolver (the real production resolver — NEVER a NoOp/Stub/in-memory nullifier, per the no-dev-stand-in tenet and #2211), applies the §9.7.1 'Resolution failure policy' Add branch (a resolution FAILURE on an AttestationTrigger::Add is a REJECT, fail-closed, with NO fallback to a stale/pre-rotation cached document), supplies check-2's resolved_at to Layer A as the clock time at which it performed that DidResolver::resolve() (so a freshly-resolved document passes Layer A's freshness gate; Layer B reads only resolve(), never a document-age field the shared resolver does not yet expose), applies the narrow testing carve-out (a positive whitelist admitting ONLY did:test: and did:key: to skip resolution, gated behind #[cfg(any(test, feature="testing"))] so it is never present in shipped production artifacts — mirroring the validate_creator_identity precedent at crates/scp-runtime/src/crypto/mls/provider.rs), and delegates to Layer A. Enforcement MUST NOT be keyed on a single method prefix such as did:dht:z — did:web:* is equally in scope and fail-closed (§9.7.1 'Fail-closed scope'). SCOPE (startable now): Layer A plus the Add-fail-closed / current-key / testing-carve-out Layer B path are genuinely completable now against merged S2, using ONLY DidResolver::resolve() and Layer A's caller-supplied resolved_at/now — they touch NO shared resolver type. Two things are deliberately EXCLUDED as boundary-stable follow-ons, NOT hard ACs here: (1) resolver-side privacy-cache freshness enforcement — that a document served from the §9.10.7 24h/7d privacy cache and older than MAX_ATTESTATION_KEY_RESOLUTION_STALENESS MUST force a fresh re-resolution — which requires the unsettled resolver-freshness seam (open question a: the canonical ResolvedDidDocument carries no resolution timestamp today, so Layer B cannot yet read a served document's age) and is the tracked SCP-CRYPTO22-005 follow-on that depends on the shared #2211 resolver; and (2) the already-admitted-member Update last-known-good grace branch (§9.7.1 'Resolution failure policy', Update bullet). Excluding these keeps every hard AC implementable within the AC10 scope boundary (scp-mls + scp-runtime only; NEVER scp-identity/src/resolver.rs). This story adds NO FFI export, NO ContextManager/Supervisor wiring, and NO pipeline_wiring.rs assertion — those are S6/S7. S1/S2 are already merged on main (S2 = PR #2246), so this story is startable with no blocking PRD story or GitHub issue — hence blockedBy/blockedByIssues are empty; there are no PRD story IDs to reference for S1/S2 (see the program-level provenance-gap observation in the PRD description).
acceptanceCriteria: Layer A is a pure, side-effect-free function added to crates/scp-mls/src/keypackage_attestation.rs whose signature takes an already-resolved scp_did::DidDocument, a resolved_at: u64, and a now: u64 (plus the remaining ground-truth leaf/credential inputs) and returns Result<(), _>; it performs NO async, NO network, and NO clock read (grep confirms the function body contains no `.await`, no resolver call, and no SystemClock/Clock::now usage), preserving scp-mls's wasm32 safety; a `cargo test -p scp-mls` unit test compiles and calls it (§9.7.1 checks 1–2; ADR-057 Amendment 'code seam').

Check-2 freshness boundary is pinned by two scp-mls unit tests against MAX_ATTESTATION_KEY_RESOLUTION_STALENESS (300s, §9.18.7): a document with now - resolved_at == 300 PASSES the freshness gate, and a document with now - resolved_at == 301 is REJECTED with the story's typed staleness error before verify_attestation is reached (§9.7.1 check 2).

Check-1 current-key rejection is pinned by scp-mls unit tests: (a) when the verification method named by the credential's signing_key_id is absent or #retired-* in the resolved current DidDocument, Layer A REJECTS with a typed current-key error and does NOT call verify_attestation; (b) when that VM is present but carries a rotated-away key, the delegated verify_attestation returns the existing AttestationVerifyError::SignatureInvalid (§9.7.1 check 1; §9.12 rotation-is-revocation).

Layer A enforces the check-2 freshness gate BEFORE the check-1 current-key extraction, which is before the delegated verify_attestation checks 3–13 — asserted by a test where a stale (301s) document that ALSO has a valid current key still fails with the staleness error, never a checks-3–13 error (§9.7.1 checks 1–2 ordering).

Layer B (scp-runtime) resolves the signer DID exclusively through a scp_identity::resolver::DidResolver value passed in via dependency injection; grep confirms the module constructs no NoOp/Stub/InMemory resolver on the production path and reads the resolver from its injected dependencies (no-dev-stand-in tenet; #2211).

Add fail-closed on resolution failure is pinned by a scp-runtime test: with an injected DidResolver that returns Err(...) or Ok(None) for the signer DID, Layer B on AttestationTrigger::Add returns a typed REJECT and never consults a stale/pre-rotation cached document (no cache-fallback code path exists on the Add branch) (§9.7.1 'Resolution failure policy' — New member (Add); ADR-057 Amendment 'Verifier').

Layer B supplies an HONEST resolved_at to Layer A, computed as the clock time at which it performed DidResolver::resolve() (read from the injected scp_clock::Clock, never a fabricated/hardcoded timestamp) — pinned by a scp-runtime test asserting a successfully resolved document is handed to Layer A with resolved_at within clock-skew tolerance of now, so it passes Layer A's check-2 gate; this uses only resolve() + the clock and touches no shared resolver type (§9.7.1 check 2; §9.14 clock-skew tolerance).

The testing carve-out is a positive whitelist admitting ONLY the did:test: and did:key: prefixes to skip DID-document resolution, and is gated behind #[cfg(any(test, feature="testing"))]; grep confirms (a) the cfg gate wraps the carve-out, (b) enforcement is NOT keyed on a did:dht:z prefix (did:web:* is not exempted), and a scp-runtime test asserts that under the testing feature a did:test: signer skips resolution while a did:web: signer does not (§9.7.1 'Fail-closed scope (positive whitelist)'; ADR-057 Amendment — mirrors validate_creator_identity at crates/scp-runtime/src/crypto/mls/provider.rs).

The pure S2 core is byte-unchanged: `git diff origin/main` shows NO modification to the body of `pub fn verify_attestation`, to AttestationVerifyError, or to the `mod tests` §25.23 Vector 37 known-answer tests (vector_37_signing_preimage_matches_spec / vector_37_signing_hash_matches_spec / vector_37_extension_body_matches_spec) in crates/scp-mls/src/keypackage_attestation.rs — S4 is additive to that module only (§9.7.1 checks 3–13 remain the unchanged pure core).

Scope boundary is enforced mechanically: `git diff --name-only origin/main` touches only crates/scp-mls/src/keypackage_attestation.rs, crates/scp-runtime/src/crypto/mls/* (the new Layer-B module + its mod.rs declaration), and this PRD file — and modifies NO file under crates/scp-ffi/, NO pipeline_wiring.rs, and NO sdk-capability-matrix.json (FFI export, ContextManager wiring, and the pipeline assertion are S6/S7) (ADR-057 Amendment — 'code … is the follow-on implementation PR').
actionItems: Read crates/scp-mls/src/keypackage_attestation.rs in full — the merged S2 caller contract on AttestationVerificationContext::resolved_current_vm_pubkey and verify_attestation's rustdoc — and crates/scp-mls/src/credential.rs::resolve_signing_key (extracts a VM pubkey by signing_key_id from a DidDocument, the reuse point for check 1).

Add Layer A to crates/scp-mls/src/keypackage_attestation.rs: a pure fn taking (attestation, resolved DidDocument, resolved_at: u64, now: u64, leaf/credential ground-truth), enforcing check 2 (freshness ≤ MAX_ATTESTATION_KEY_RESOLUTION_STALENESS) then check 1 (current-VM extract via resolve_signing_key; reject absent/#retired-*) then delegating unchanged to verify_attestation. Add a typed staleness error variant/error type; do NOT edit verify_attestation, AttestationVerifyError, or the Vector 37 tests.
Add scp-mls unit tests: the 300/301 freshness boundary; absent/#retired-* current VM rejection; rotated-key → SignatureInvalid; and the check-2-before-check-1-before-3–13 ordering test.

Add Layer B module crates/scp-runtime/src/crypto/mls/attestation_verification.rs and declare it in crates/scp-runtime/src/crypto/mls/mod.rs: an async fn that resolves via an injected scp_identity::resolver::DidResolver, applies the Add fail-closed policy (Err/None ⇒ typed REJECT, no stale fallback), supplies resolved_at = the injected clock's time at the resolve() call to Layer A, applies the #[cfg(any(test, feature="testing"))] did:test:/did:key: positive-whitelist carve-out (mirroring provider.rs::validate_creator_identity), then delegates to Layer A. Do NOT touch crates/scp-identity/src/resolver.rs — the resolver-side privacy-cache freshness enforcement is the SCP-CRYPTO22-005 follow-on (details.followOn), not this story.

Add scp-runtime tests: resolver returns Err/None on Add ⇒ REJECT with no cache fallback; a successful resolve hands Layer A a resolved_at within skew of now (honest, clock-derived); testing carve-out skips did:test: but not did:web: under the testing feature; and DidResolver is injected (no NoOp/Stub constructed on the production path).

Run local CI before pushing: `cargo clippy -p scp-mls -p scp-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p scp-mls`, `cargo test -p scp-runtime` (with DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH), and the scp-runtime check-*.sh gate set; confirm `git diff --name-only origin/main` matches the scope-boundary AC.

Leave the resolver-side privacy-cache freshness enforcement (details.followOn / SCP-CRYPTO22-005) and the Update last-known-good grace branch OUT of this story entirely — 004's Layer B derives resolved_at from the clock at resolve() and never inspects a cached document's age, so it needs no ResolvedDidDocument age field and touches no shared resolver type. Author SCP-CRYPTO22-005 only after open question (a) is settled.

sources.section: ## Amendment (2026-08-01): Ephemeral MLS leaf key + DID attestation (leaf-binding)

mergedPredecessors.S1: pure 0xFF03 data type + §9.5.1 serialization + §25.23 Vector 37 KAT (on main)

openQuestions: Resolver-seam freshness-extension shape (awaits human confirmation): the canonical ResolvedDidDocument (crates/scp-identity/src/resolver.rs) currently carries NO resolution timestamp, so Layer B cannot yet read the age of a document served from cache. Two additive options — (a) add a resolve_fresh(did, max_staleness) method to the DidResolver trait, or (b) add a resolved_at field to ResolvedDidDocument — both touch the shared #2211 resolver and MUST be settled upstream before the resolver-side privacy-cache freshness enforcement can be wired. Because this seam is unsettled upstream, that enforcement is NOT a hard AC of SCP-CRYPTO22-004 (which would otherwise contradict its own scope boundary); it is the SCP-CRYPTO22-005 follow-on below. SCP-CRYPTO22-004's ACs are scoped so they hold under either choice.

Whether the already-admitted-member Update last-known-good grace branch (§9.7.1 'Resolution failure policy', Update bullet — bounded §9.10.7 retention, degrading toward the MAX_KEYPACKAGE_ATTESTATION_LIFETIME backstop under a rollback-capable attacker) lands in a follow-on or defers to S7. This story deliberately scopes its hard ACs to the Add fail-closed + current-key path only; the Update grace is a noted boundary, not an AC.
details.followOn: SCP-CRYPTO22-005 (to be authored once resolver-freshness seam shape — open question a — is settled; depends on the shared #2211 resolver): resolver-side privacy-cache freshness enforcement — a DID document served from the §9.10.7 24h/7d privacy cache and older than MAX_ATTESTATION_KEY_RESOLUTION_STALENESS (§9.18.7, 300s) MUST force a fresh re-resolution and MUST NOT satisfy the attestation current-key check (§9.7.1 check 2). Deliberately NOT authored here: it cannot be implemented within SCP-CRYPTO22-004's scope boundary because it requires editing crates/scp-identity/src/resolver.rs (the ResolvedDidDocument age seam), which the unsettled #2211 upstream governs.
details.provenanceGapObservation: S1–S3 shipped without PRD stories (program-level provenance gap). Retroactively authoring those is out of scope for this artifact and is NOT fabricated here.
